PubMed confirms CMAJ, 2001, Review. key_finding and relevance_to_tphe are accurate. TIER OVERCLAIM: evidence_level asserted CMAJ is 'Lancet/BMJ/JAMA-tier' — CMAJ is a well-respected leading national general-medical journal but is not conventionally ranked alongside the NEJM/Lancet/JAMA/BMJ 'big-4' by impact factor or citation standing. Corrected evidence_level written into source file: describes CMAJ as a leading national general-medical journal without the direct Lancet/BMJ/JAMA equivalence claim.

PubMed confirms JAMA Network Open, 2025, RCT pubtype confirmed, cluster RCT of 8 mosque clusters/5 districts as described. FINDING: the record's key_finding claims 'full effect sizes in abstract are truncated in the fetched record' — this is FALSE; the full PubMed abstract contains complete numeric results (T2D incidence 9.8% vs 17.1%, ARR 7.3pp, RRR 42.5%, adjusted HR 0.75 [95% CI 0.60-0.95], P=.02, plus improved secondary metabolic outcomes). Corrected key_finding with the actual effect sizes written into source file, per the strict effect-size requirement for RCT outcomes.

PubMed confirms JAMA Network Open, 2024, RCT pubtype confirmed, n=101 Somali refugees, Seattle/Columbus, 12-week follow-up as described. FINDING: the record's key_finding claims 'numeric effect sizes truncated in fetched abstract' — this is FALSE; the full abstract reports Cohen's d for all three primary/secondary outcomes (PTSD severity d=-0.67, depression d=-0.66, well-being d=0.71), maintained at 12-week follow-up. Corrected key_finding with the actual effect sizes written into source file.

PubMed confirms Medical Decision Making, 2024, quasi-experimental pre/post design (not RCT) as described. FINDING: key_finding calls the ultra-Orthodox reluctance 'adjusted OR 0.23' — the abstract reports OR=0.23 (P<.001, parents) and OR=0.43 (P<.001, young adults) with NO statement that these are covariate-adjusted; the design is quasi-experimental pre/post with no stated adjustment model, so 'adjusted' is an unsupported strengthening of the claim. Also omitted from the record: the abstract separately reports an increased vaccination inclination among Muslim-Arab participants (OR=3.12, P<.001), directly relevant to T-PHE's population. Corrected key_finding (dropping 'adjusted', adding the young-adult OR and the Muslim-Arab finding, and naming the quasi-experimental design) written into source file.

PubMed confirms Nursing in Critical Care, 2026, Systematic Review pubtype confirmed. Abstract: 52 studies (30/58% high quality), PRISMA 2020, stressors (uncertainty, restricted visitation, financial burden, cultural/linguistic barriers) and needs (emotional reassurance, spiritual guidance, communication, decision-making involvement) — matches key_finding exactly. Correctly flagged ICU-vs-premarital-counseling setting mismatch as an analogy caveat.

PubMed confirms Trauma, Violence & Abuse, 2025. PubMed's own PublicationType tag is 'Review' rather than 'Systematic Review', but the abstract explicitly describes a PRISMA-guided review of 332 screened / 25 included studies with a mixed-methods appraisal tool — methodologically a systematic review as the record states, so not treated as a tier overclaim. IPV as most prevalent form, spirituality/rights-knowledge protective, husband's-control/economic-dependence risk factors — matches key_finding precisely, including the record's own caution against romanticizing family/marital authority.

PubMed confirms Reproductive Health, 2020, Systematic Review pubtype confirmed, 59 studies/22 countries. Abstract: poor SRH knowledge/negative attitudes, husband/family opposition, fear of stigmatization re: premarital sexual relations as barriers — matches key_finding directly. relevance_to_tphe is directly on-topic and reasonably balances 'family involvement is protective' against 'family opposition is a barrier.'

PubMed confirms Human Fertility, 2015, self-labeled 'Systematic review of the literature' (Medline 1978-2013), Systematic Review pubtype confirmed. Abstract: ART permitted only within an intact marriage, surrogacy/third-party donation forbidden, gender selection permitted for medical reasons (limited social reasons by some jurists) — matches key_finding exactly. Note: this is a review of jurisprudential/legal literature, not clinical-outcomes evidence, but the record does not misrepresent it as the latter.

PubMed confirms Journal of Religion and Health, 2022, Systematic Review pubtype confirmed, 162/1858 studies screened. Abstract: growth from 5 to 73 studies per 5-year period 2000-2019, only 7% higher quality, mixed beneficial/adverse findings — matches key_finding exactly, including the 7% figure. Correctly labeled as a cross-population analogy (mainland China, largely non-Muslim) used for methodological caution, not direct evidence.

PubMed confirms Journal of Religion and Health, 2019, Meta-Analysis pubtype confirmed, 10 Arabic-language studies. Abstract: all correlations negative, mean effect size r=-0.22 (range -0.16 to -0.43), age/gender not significant moderators — matches key_finding's effect-size claim exactly, correctly caveated as a small-to-moderate correlation, not causal proof, satisfying the strict-effect-size requirement for this angle.

PubMed confirms Burns, 2021, Systematic Review pubtype confirmed, 7 of 236 screened qualitative papers. Abstract: marital/familial conflict, male-dominated culture, mental-health disorders, economic/social factors as drivers; social isolation/regret/physical-psychological harm as consequences — matches key_finding exactly. relevance_to_tphe reasonably uses this as a caution against romanticizing family/marital authority, not as direct T-PHE outcome evidence.

PubMed confirms Frontiers in Neurology, 2025. key_finding (stepwise Hoehn-and-Yahr-stratified fasting algorithm) matches the abstract. TIER OVERCLAIM: PubMed's own PublicationType tag is 'Review', not 'Practice Guideline' — the paper synthesizes an existing guideline (BIMA Ramadan Compendium) plus a professional-society consensus meeting and expert opinion, which is consensus-level guidance but not itself a formally PubMed-classified clinical practice guideline. Additionally, Frontiers in Neurology is a high-volume, broad-scope journal with more variable editorial selectivity than a dedicated specialty journal, so calling it a 'leading specialty journal' overstates its standing. Corrected evidence_level written into source file, downgrading the tier claim while keeping the record (still usable as expert-consensus-level evidence).

overall_note: 20/20 PMIDs resolve on NCBI PubMed with matching title, journal, and year. 15/20 records verified as-is (KEEP). 5/20 required correction and were rewritten in the source file: (1) PMID 11202669 overclaimed CMAJ as 'Lancet/BMJ/JAMA-tier' rather than a leading-but-not-big-4 journal; (2) PMID 41114978 and (3) PMID 39186273 both falsely claimed their RCT effect sizes were 'truncated' when the full numeric results (risk reductions, hazard ratio, Cohen's d) are present in the PubMed abstract — corrected to state the actual effect sizes per this angle's strict effect-size requirement; (4) PMID 38600776 mislabeled a crude odds ratio from a quasi-experimental (non-randomized) pre/post study as 'adjusted' and omitted the Muslim-Arab subgroup finding (OR=3.12) directly relevant to T-PHE's population; (5) PMID 41458120 overclaimed a Frontiers in Neurology narrative review (PubMed pubtype 'Review', not 'Practice Guideline') as an 'explicit professional/clinical consensus guideline' in a 'leading specialty journal' without qualification. The two Journal of IMA carve-out records (23610513, 23864762) were checked against the carve-out instruction and found already self-labeled correctly, so no FIX was required there. No record was dropped: all 20 pass exists/title/year verification, all key findings that could be checked against the retrieved abstract text are supported (after the 5 corrections above), all tier claims are true or have been corrected to be true, and all relevance-to-T-PHE claims are reasonable interpretive mappings that do not present ethics/opinion papers as outcome evidence and do label cross-population items as analogies.
